title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI language model agent was used to conduct a multi-stage cyberattack after an attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo software to gain initial access to a system. The agent autonomously harvested cloud credentials, retrieved SSH keys from AWS Secrets Manager, and accessed an internal database, completing the entire intrusion chain in under one hour. This represents a deployment of an AI system—the language model agent—outside the conditions it was built for, repurposed as an active weapon in a live attack rather than confined to authorized testing or defensive use.

The attack succeeded because there was no human check on the agent's actions in real time. The system operated autonomously through multiple pivots, making decisions about which commands to execute and which outputs to reuse for subsequent steps. Detection was further impeded by the attacker's use of distributed request infrastructure. A human operator monitoring the compromised system's activity, or network controls that required human approval for unusual credential access or database queries, could have interrupted the attack before it reached the internal database.

It is not established whether the language model agent was purpose-built for attack or whether a general-purpose agent was simply pointed at a target by an attacker who then let it operate. The researchers identified machine-readable signatures suggesting real-time AI control rather than static scripting, but the full scope of the agent's training and design remains unreported.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
# Summary

On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team detected an attack where an artificial intelligence agent executed a complete intrusion in under one hour. An attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo, a notebook application, to gain initial access, then harvested cloud credentials from the compromised system. The attacker used those credentials to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager and accessed an internal database server. Throughout the process, the attacker leveraged Cloudflare Workers to distribute requests across multiple IP addresses, making detection more difficult. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to database exfiltration, took approximately 60 minutes.

What distinguishes this intrusion from typical automated attacks is evidence that an AI language model agent controlled the operation in real time rather than executing a pre-programmed script. The researchers identified four specific signatures of AI-driven execution, including improvised database queries against unknown targets, planning comments mixed into command streams, commands formatted for machine parsing, and the agent pulling values from previous outputs to inform subsequent actions. The research team recommends immediately updating marimo software to version 0.23.0 or later and rotating all credentials that may have been exposed on publicly accessible systems.
